sources: The $1.5B acquisition adds AI-driven customer data capabilities to Diginex's sustainability and compliance platform — transforming it from a point solution into an integrated end-to-end platform.
prompt:
TESSERA STYLE SHEET
1. Modern editorial paper collage: bold magazine composition, refined 2D motion design, photographed flat under soft room light.
2. One flat block-colour paper ground fills the frame: soft violet. The ground is a single unbroken colour.
3. Subjects are black-and-white halftone photographic cutouts with rough white torn-paper edges: objects, machines, buildings, maps, coins, screens, vehicles, anonymous paper hands. Every cutout is a plain, unmarked object: calendar pages, documents, coins, screens and vehicles are blank and unprinted, with no lettering, numerals, symbols, liveries or marks on them.
4. Diagram elements are flat matte paper shapes and ribbons in cream, black, pale yellow, or the ground's contrasting colour, with real paper texture, print dots and small pieces of tape.
5. One consistent light from the upper left; each paper layer casts a small soft shadow.
6. Every surface is matte printed paper reflecting only the room light: cutouts, chips, ribbons and ground all read as photographed paper, with the same flat finish edge to edge. No glow, neon, bloom or halo anywhere.
7. Layout: the headline chip owns the upper third of the frame and stays uncovered; subjects and diagrams occupy the lower two-thirds. When the frame opens on a previous composition, its elements slide off or are covered in the first second and the new headline lands on clear ground.
8. Headline typography: one extra-bold sans-serif in black or cream, printed on a cream or black paper chip, large, with safe margins. Letterforms are accurate, complete and stable from the frame they appear in; the chip is printed once and does not redraw.
9. Motion: elements enter fast with slight overshoot and a stable landing, then hold a clear reading window; one strongest focus at a time; the camera is locked; movement starts on the first frame and a small loop continues at the end; no empty frames.
10. 16:9, exactly 5 seconds, one composition, at most one crisp cut.
11. Identity anchor: rough white torn edges on every cutout; small paper shadow from the upper-left light.

BEAT
Ground: soft violet.
Subjects: two paper tiles; a strip of tape.
Opens on the screen, carried over from the previous shot, which transforms as the action begins.
Action: The previous chip slides off the top edge as the screen splits into two paper tiles; tape binds them into one panel.
Ends holding on the bound panel.
Headline printed on a paper chip: "END-TO-END".

ON-SCREEN TEXT: "END-TO-END". This string is printed complete and correct from its first visible frame and never changes. It is the only lettering in the frame.

AUDIO: One English narrator, warm, clear, natural, brisk but unhurried, never an advertising shout. Speak the following line exactly once, word for word, beginning on the first frame: "Diginex moves from a point solution to an integrated platform.". No other dialogue. Light paper-slap and tape sound effects beneath the voice; no music.
expandedPrompt:
For the target video, at 0.00 seconds into the target video, <Picture 1> (from [Shot 1]) is fully referenced.

integrated_multimodal_description: [Shot 1] This is a modern editorial paper collage in a cinematic, photographed-flat style, as established in <Picture 1>. The scene opens on a soft violet block-color paper ground. In the upper third of the frame, a cream paper chip with the bold black text "$1.5B" is visible, and in the lower two-thirds, a black-and-white halftone photographic cutout of a stack of blank coins and a blank white screen are positioned against the ground. All cutouts feature rough white torn-paper edges and cast small, soft shadows from a consistent light source in the upper left. On the first frame, a warm, clear, natural English-speaking narrator (S1) says, <d>[English] Diginex moves from a point solution to an integrated platform.</d> Simultaneously, the camera remains in a Static Shot as the cream "$1.5B" chip and the coin cutout slide quickly off the top and left edges of the frame with a slight overshoot. From the center, the blank white screen splits cleanly into two identical rectangular paper tiles. Immediately, a strip of semi-transparent matte paper tape slides across the seam, binding the two tiles into a single integrated panel. Simultaneously, a new cream paper chip slides in from the top, landing stably in the upper third of the frame. Printed on this chip in a large, extra-bold black sans-serif font is the text "END-TO-END", which remains clean, legible, and stable. The video ends with a hold on this composition: the "END-TO-END" headline above and the tape-bound panel below, all maintaining their matte paper textures and soft shadows.

overall_soundscape: The audio features the clear, professional voice of a narrator. Beneath the speech, there are synchronized diegetic sound effects: a crisp, light paper-slap as the elements slide and land, and a tactile, sticky ripping and pressing sound as the tape binds the tiles together.
